holidays.name: National Hat Day
holidays.description: A day to dust off your favorite headwear, from fedoras and beanies to wacky novelty hats, and wear it proudly all day long. Bonus points for anything with a propeller or a cheese wedge.
holidays.origin: National Hat Day is an unofficial observance that became popular in the United States in the 2000s, promoted through social media and lists of national days. No single founder is clearly documented.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'mad as a hatter' is often linked to 18th and 19th century hat makers who suffered mercury poisoning from the chemicals used in felting.

holidays.name: National Bagel Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the chewy, boiled-then-baked ring of carb perfection. Cream cheese, lox, everything seasoning, or even pizza bagels are all welcome at this breakfast bash.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food holiday that grew in popularity in the US, tied to the bagel's history among Jewish communities in Poland, where the earliest known mention dates to 1610 in Kraków.
holidays.funFact: Traditional bagels are boiled in water before baking, which gives them their signature shiny crust and dense, chewy texture.

holidays.name: Strawberry Ice Cream Day
holidays.description: A day for scooping up the pink, creamy classic. Fans argue over whether the best version has real fruit chunks or is smooth and dreamy.
holidays.origin: An unofficial food observance that circulates among national day calendars, celebrating one of the three flavors in classic Neapolitan ice cream.
holidays.funFact: Vanilla, chocolate, and strawberry make up Neapolitan ice cream, named after immigrants from Naples, Italy who popularized the layered treat in the US.

holidays.name: Wikipedia Day
holidays.description: Fans of the free online encyclopedia celebrate by editing articles, falling down rabbit holes, and thanking the volunteers who keep the world's knowledge up to date.
holidays.origin: Wikipedia was launched on January 15, 2001 by Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger, and the anniversary has been celebrated by editors ever since.
holidays.funFact: Wikipedia now exists in over 300 languages, and its volunteer editors have written millions of articles in English alone.

holidays.name: Humanitarian Day (Martin Luther King Jr. Birthday Eve Quirk: Bunny Day Alternative) - Hat Trick Day
holidays.description: A playful unofficial observance of tricks, treats, and triumphs, where people try something clever or silly three times in a row.
holidays.origin: Loosely inspired by sports and magic culture where a 'hat trick' means achieving three of something in a row, popularized informally online alongside National Hat Day.
holidays.funFact: The term 'hat trick' originated in 19th century cricket, when a bowler who took three wickets in a row was awarded a new hat.
